title: Order Resolution Program Manager
description:
Positition:

The Order Resolution Program Manager builds and leads the Order Resolution Program (ORP), a national program that helps ensure patients receive the testing their physicians have ordered. When an order encounters a barrier, such as an unreachable patient, an incorrect phone number, a patient with unanswered questions about their test, or a step that requires clinic involvement, this role makes sure the right people take the right action so care is not delayed. Many of these patients are navigating a cancer diagnosis, and the program exists to support them and the Patient Coordinators who care for them.

As the program's founding owner, the Program Manager exercises independent judgment to assess the current landscape, resolve complex cases directly, and determine what the program needs to succeed, including whether and how to expand the team. The role is hands-on by design: the Program Manager works open cases alongside Patient Coordinators to understand where and why orders stall, then uses that firsthand insight and program data to set strategy, define standards, and guide leadership decisions.

The Program Manager partners across Patient Services, Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Patient Coordinators, Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers, earning alignment through expertise and sound judgment rather than direct authority.

 

Primary Responsibilities:

Program Strategy & Ownership

  • Own the Order Resolution Program end-to-end across all national regions, independently assessing the current landscape, including case volume, root causes, regional variation, and existing workflows, to determine where patient orders are most at risk of delay.
  • Develop a data-supported program roadmap and staffing recommendation for Patient Services leadership, including headcount requirements, staffing structure, timeline, and whether process or tooling solutions would better serve patients.
  • Define the program operating model, including case ownership, escalation criteria, service timelines, handoff protocols, and quality standards, and adjust it as the program matures.
  • Lead the design of the team structure, role definitions, hiring profile, onboarding, and performance expectations for future team members.

Case Resolution & Patient Care Support

  • Exercise independent judgment to evaluate open ORP cases, determine the root cause of each barrier, and develop a tailored resolution strategy that accounts for the clinical context, the patient's circumstances, and available resources.
  • Work complex and high-priority cases directly, including researching LIMS, paper orders, and patient outreach tools to locate missing or updated contact information, and decide whether a case calls for administrative resolution, clinic education or engagement, or escalation.
  • Partner with Patient Coordinators to support patient outreach, providing guidance on how to approach each case and, where appropriate, connecting with patients directly so that questions about their orders are answered and care can move forward.
  • Determine when to escalate a case to the clinic, engage the field team, or close it, and document the rationale so any subsequent owner can continue seamlessly.
  • Maintain a real-time view of all open cases, including status, owner, next action, and age, and follow up consistently to confirm actions are completed and patients are not left waiting.

Analytics & Performance Reporting

  • Design, build, and maintain the ORP reporting infrastructure, including dashboards, KPI scorecards, and regional trend analysis, and define the metrics used to measure program success.
  • Report regularly to Patient Services leadership on case volume, resolution rates, time to resolution, and order completion outcomes, translating data into clear insights about what is working, what is not, and what should change.
  • Analyze recurring barriers, such as common reasons patients cannot be reached or questions that arise repeatedly, and develop recommendations that reduce the number of patients whose orders require intervention in the first place.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Process Improvement

  • Partner with Territory Managers, Clinical Oncology Specialists, Associate Clinical Oncology Specialists, and Patient Coordinators to set clear expectations, communicate promptly, and share accountability on every open case.
  • Partner with Inside Sales Managers, Regional Directors, and Operations Managers to align program priorities, resolve regional barriers, and ensure teams understand their role in supporting patient orders.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert for ORP, providing guidance and consultation to field and operations partners and developing best practices, training, and standard work that can be adopted nationally.
  • Identify systemic process gaps and bring structured, data-backed recommendations to leadership, including changes to workflows, status definitions, tooling, and cross-team handoffs, with the patient experience as the guiding lens.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

 

Qualifications:

 

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, life sciences, or a related field; or equivalent professional experience in a role requiring independent judgment, program ownership, and decision-making in a healthcare or clinical operations environment.
  • 5 or more years of experience in healthcare operations, patient services, program or project management, or a comparable environment, with demonstrated ownership of a program, workflow, or initiative from assessment through execution.
  • Demonstrated ability to assess a complex operating landscape, identify root causes, and develop and present a data-supported recommendation, including resourcing and staffing needs, to senior leadership.
  • Proven ability to independently assess multi-variable situations and determine the appropriate course of action without direct supervision, particularly in patient-facing or clinically sensitive contexts.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and drive accountability across cross-functional teams, including field, sales, and operations leaders, without direct authority.
  • Strong analytical capability, including building performance reporting, interpreting trends, and communicating findings clearly to leadership; advanced MS Excel or equivalent skills required.
  • Experience in a call center, patient outreach, or high-volume case management environment (inbound and outbound).
  • Proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and data tools; familiarity with skip tracing tools and LIMS is a strong plus.
  • Prior experience leading, coaching, or building a team is preferred. Background in patient coordination or another patient-facing healthcare role is strongly preferred.

 

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Technical

  • Program and project management expertise, including scoping, planning, prioritization, milestone tracking, and stakeholder management.
  • Specialized knowledge of healthcare operations, patient services workflows, and clinical coordination sufficient to evaluate case scenarios and develop resolution strategies without relying on standardized scripts.
  • Advanced proficiency in CRM platforms, case tracking systems, and reporting tools, with the ability to design KPI dashboards that give leadership real-time visibility into program performance and patient order outcomes.
  • Strong quantitative skills, including comfort working with large data sets to identify trends, build business cases, and model staffing and capacity needs.
  • Experience with skip tracing tools and multi-database research methods, and with process documentation and standard operating procedure development.

Behavioral

  • Exercises sound, independent judgment consistently, treating each case and each program decision as a situation requiring individualized analysis.
  • Builds before being asked: sees what a new program needs, takes ownership of the decision, and moves forward without waiting to be told something is off track.
  • Balances urgency and care: moves quickly because patients are waiting, and makes thoughtful decisions because the stakes are real.
  • Thinks like a program owner and acts like a teammate: comfortable working individual cases to learn the work, and equally comfortable stepping back to set strategy and advise leadership.
  • Earns credibility with cross-functional partners through expertise, clear communication, and follow-through, and uses it to drive action across teams they do not directly control.
  • Coaches and develops others, and is ready to build and lead a team as the program grows.

 

Physical Demands & Work Environment:

  • This is a primarily remote position. Occasional on-site attendance may be required for planning sessions, leadership reviews, or business needs.
  • Duties are performed in a home office or professional office setting and require the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone, and read printed and digital material.
  • This role may require working outside standard business hours at times to address time-sensitive case situations or program needs.

Travel:

Minimal travel required. Occasional travel (estimated less than 15%) may be required for national leadership meetings, regional business reviews, or planning sessions.

One Platform. One Profit Engine.

  • Reporting: Du hilfst beim Erstellen von Präsentationen und Reportings, mit denen Performance-Kennzahlen und strategische Initiativen ans Management gehen.
  • Teamarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit Team-Leads, Disponenten und dem Ops-Management zusammen und begleitest laufende Projekte.

 

Was du mitbringst

Must-have

  • Studium in BWL, Wirtschaftswissenschaften, (Wirtschafts-)Ingenieurwesen, Logistik, Data oder einem verwandten Bereich, oder Abschluss bereits in der Tasche
  • Analytisches und strukturiertes Denken kombiniert mit einer Hands-on-Mentalität
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Zahlen und Daten; Excel und PowerPoint sind selbstverständlich
  • KI-affine Arbeitsweise, du nutzt Tools wie Claude, ChatGPT oder Gemini aktiv im Alltag
  • Deutsch C1 und Englisch C1, beide Sprachen gehören zum Arbeitsalltag

Nice to have

  • Erste Erfahrung im Consulting, Business Development, Operations oder einem datengetriebenen Umfeld
  • SQL oder erste Erfahrung mit BI-Tools
  • Interesse an oder Erfahrung mit der Automobilbranche

  • Regelmäßige Feedbackzyklen
  • Frisches Obst und Getränke im Büro
  • Laptop für mobiles Arbeiten

Wir besetzen aktuell mehrere Praktika im Operations-Umfeld. Wenn sich im Gespräch zeigt, dass ein anderer Bereich besser zu dir passt, sprechen wir darüber.

 

Bewirb dich jetzt – dein Lebenslauf reicht.

Support investigations into unexpected results, process variation, material issues, and non-conformances. Maintain laboratory organisation, stock levels, equipment readiness, waste handling, and safety standards. What we are looking for Experience working in a laboratory, chemical-processing, manufacturing, or other practical technical environment. A technical qualification or practical training in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, laboratory science, or a related field. Practical understanding of laboratory safety, chemical handling, personal protective equipment, and safe working procedures. Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow written procedures consistently. A collaborative, reliable, and proactive approach to working with engineers, scientists, technicians, and production teams. Desirable experience Solid rocket propellants, energetic materials, polymers, binders, oxidisers, metallic fuels, or catalysts. Laboratory-scale mixing, casting, curing, grinding, sample preparation, or chemical processing. Propellant characterisation, burn-rate measurement, thermal analysis, rheology, mechanical testing, or compatibility testing. Experience with laboratory equipment, calibration, maintenance, or troubleshooting. Chemical inventory management, incoming-material inspection, supplier samples, or non-conformance investigations. Experience working with hazardous chemicals, explosives, regulated materials, or formal laboratory quality systems.   • Previous computer experience.

Working closely with the Lead Propellant Manager, laboratory technicians, propulsion engineers, manufacturing, and suppliers, you will define and execute quality-control activities from incoming raw materials through to finished propellant. This is a hands-on role for someone who combines strong technical judgement with a disciplined approach to measurement, documentation, investigation, and process control. Your work will help ensure that propellant development and production remain safe, repeatable, and aligned with the required performance standards. About us We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket. We are working hard to build something truly spectacular. To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you. At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Define and perform quality-control checks for raw materials, intermediate products, and finished propellant. Develop and maintain inspection plans, test methods, acceptance criteria, sampling requirements, and quality records. Review laboratory and production data to identify trends, variation, out-of-specification results, and emerging process issues. Lead or support investigations into non-conformances, deviations, material issues, and unexpected test results. Maintain clear traceability of materials, batches, samples, equipment, results, and technical decisions. Work with the Lead Propellant Manager and manufacturing teams to improve process capability, measurement quality, and production consistency. What we are looking for Experience in quality control, quality engineering, laboratory testing, or process control within a chemical, aerospace, manufacturing, or other regulated environment. A degree in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline. Strong understanding of measurement systems, test methods, sampling, data review, and technical documentation. Experience investigating non-conformances, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions. A methodical and detail-oriented approach to safety, traceability, data integrity, and compliance. Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with laboratory, engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supplier teams. Desirable experience Solid rocket propellants, energetic materials, Elastomers, polymers, binders, oxidisers, metallic fuels, or catalysts. Propellant or chemical-material characterisation, including thermal, mechanical, rheological, chemical, or burn-rate testing. Incoming-material inspection, supplier quality, batch release, certificate-of-analysis review, or material qualification. Statistical process control, measurement-system analysis, capability studies, trend analysis, or uncertainty assessment. Experience with hazardous chemicals, explosives, regulated materials, or formal laboratory and manufacturing quality systems. Python, MATLAB, laboratory information systems, electronic records, or other tools for quality and test-data analysis. Benefits and important information: We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent. Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success. Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas. Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday Free access to shared company housing Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week. We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger. title: Growth Marketing Specialist
description:
About Avalere Health

United by one profound purpose: to reach EVERY PATIENT POSSIBLE. At Avalere Health, we ensure every patient is identified, treated, supported, and cared for. Equally. Our Advisory, Medical, and Marketing teams come together – powerfully and intentionally – to forge unconventional connections, building a future where healthcare is not a barrier and no patient is left behind. 

Achieving our mission starts with providing enriching, purpose-driven careers for our team that empower them to make a tangible impact on patient lives. We are committed to creating a culture where our employees are empowered to bring their whole selves to work and tap into the power of diverse backgrounds and skillsets to play a part in making a difference for every patient, everywhere. 

Our flexible approach to working allows our global teams to decide where they want to work, whether in-office or at home based on team and client need. Major city hubs in London, Manchester, Washington, D.C., and New York, and smaller offices globally, serve as collaboration hubs allowing our teams to come together when it matters. Homeworkers are equally supported, with dedicated social opportunities and resources.  

Our inclusive culture is at the heart of everything we do. We proudly support our employees in bringing their whole selves to work with our six Employee Network Groups – Diverse Ability, Family, Gender, LGBTQ+, Mental Health, and Race/Ethnicity. These groups provide opportunities to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and to connect, learn, and socialise through regular meetings and programs of activity. We are an accredited Fertility Friendly employer with our Fertility Policy, enhanced parental leave, and culture of flexibility ensuring every employee feels supported across their family planning journey and can work in a way that suits their family’s needs. 

We are deeply invested in supporting professional growth for our employees through day-to-day career experiences, access to thousands of on-demand training sessions, regular career conversations, and the opportunity for global, cross-capability career moves.  

We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you'd like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.


The Role
 
The Growth Marketing Specialist role is a hands-on, delivery-focused position that keeps our new business engine running day to day. Sitting at the centre of the growth team, the role supports lead generation and prospect research and owns the practical running of our pitch and proposal processes  timelines, resourcing support, submissions and deadlines. Reporting to the Associate Growth Director, the role works closely with Client Services and the cross functional team (Strategy, Creative, Corporate Marketing) to ensure every opportunity is delivered on time, on brief and consistently to a high standard.
 What we can offer You'll receive up to a 7% pension contribution, life insurance, income protection, and private medical insurance for peace of mind. Enjoy flexible working arrangements, including flexible hybrid working, along with the option to work from anywhere across the globe two weeks each year. We provide 25 days of annual leave plus two personal well-being days, along with gifted end-of-year holidays and an early Summer Friday finish in June, July, and August. Access free counselling through our employee assistance program, as well as personalized health support. Enhanced maternity, paternity, family leave, and fertility policies provide support across every stage of your family-planning journey, as well as on-demand support from our partner Peppy. You can also benefit from continuous opportunities to professionally develop with on-demand training, support, and global mobility opportunities across the business. We encourage all applicants to read our candidate privacy notice before applying to Avalere Health.

description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
 
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
 
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
 
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.


The Role 
Veeva is looking for a highly motivated individual with life science industry experience within the Safety (Pharmacovigilance) domain to drive customer success with our Veeva Safety Suite products.
 
As part of the Veeva Safety product team and collaborating with broader global Product Experts, your experience will play a key role in the Product organization. You will:
Build and nurture highly engaged user communities by maintaining regular communication across various forums to deliver clear, impactful messaging that drives shared understanding, encourages product adoption, and enhances customer value
Represent the Product organization in customer meetings, online communities, with internal team education and at industry events – driving increased customer value through release education and product capability promotion
Serve as the Voice of the Customer, capturing their needs and industry intelligence before sharing insights with product managers.  This helps to guide product decisions and design improvements, ultimately delivering better Safety solutions that drive regulatory compliance and operational efficiency
Develop rich relationships with key product users / influencers 
Collaborate effectively with Veeva field teams to drive customer success, product excellence, best practices (Good Vault Practice) and Veeva success! 
This role is ideal for someone passionate about Pharmacovigilance, eager to collaborate with customers, and excited to drive their success.

title: EH&S Lead
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

As EH&S Lead, you will own the development, implementation, and the management of Arc’s Environmental, Health, and Safety programs and culture. You will design solutions that satisfy overlapping local, state, and federal requirements, and serve as Arc’s primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies.

Your remit covers chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance, medical and hazardous waste, and Arc’s safety permits and sustainability programs. You will hire and manage a biosafety manager and direct the work of outside vendors and consultants.

About you

  • You are deeply committed to the health and safety of your colleagues, and you achieve it through partnership with the labs rather than around them.
  • You are genuinely curious about the science here and want to understand the research at a real level of depth.
  • You thrive in a diverse environment and enjoy working with scientists and students from many backgrounds.
  • You are energized by building programs and forging cross-functional partnerships that strengthen the community and the mission.

In this position you will

  • Provide safety leadership and EH&S subject matter expertise aligned with Arc’s operating principles.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and systems in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, driving continuous improvement.
  • Develop Arc’s safety strategy and carry out safety policies and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
  • Hire, manage, and develop a biosafety manager, setting clear priorities and standards for their work.
  • Advise Arc’s administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations.
  • Define Arc’s approach to  EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement.
  • Own and evolve Arc’s compliance programs including, but not limited to, the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and biosafety program, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.
  • Own Arc’s environmental compliance strategy, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting.
  • Own risk assessment program and conduct regular risk assessments and safety audits to identify workplace hazards — chemical, physical, biological, industrial, and radiological among them — and remediate hazards or recommend improvements to reduce them.
  • Lead investigations of accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures.
  • Conduct safety inspections and walkthroughs that deliver meaningful insight and surface continuous improvement opportunities across Arc’s labs.
  • Develop and manage EH&S management systems covering chemical inventories, SDS, near-miss reporting, permitting compliance, and incident investigations.
  • Oversee regulated medical and hazardous waste programs, including vendor contracting.
  • Act as primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies and government authorities.
  • Own procurement and maintenance of safety equipment and supply inventory, ensuring onsite personnel are adequately protected from workplace hazards.
  • Respond to emergency situations involving hazardous materials.
  • Develop, own and maintain Arc’s EH&S wiki.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in industrial hygiene, biology, chemistry, environmental science, occupational safety and health, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Master’s degree preferred.
  • 8+ years of laboratory experience, including 5 years in EH&S, with a minimum of 2 years leading and developing EH&S programs.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a track record of managing multiple projects accurately and on time.
  • Working knowledge of the scientific and technical aspects of applicable regulations — including Cal/OSHA, CalEPA, the Medical Waste Management Act, EPA, DEA, OSHA, NRC, and NFPA — and how they bear on laboratory operations.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritize resources, influence group behavior, and build consensus around safety practice.
  • Able to work independently and as part of a dynamic team, with a positive attitude, a strong sense of urgency, and a bias toward action.
  • Interest in learning new techniques, keeping accurate records, and working within established policies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing people, including hiring, coaching, and developing direct reports.
  • Demonstrated success leading change management in a research or lab environment.
  • Experience with Animal Research Occupational Health and Safety programs.
  • Experience supporting laboratory animal research involving biohazardous or hazardous materials.
  • Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) certification.

The base salary range for this position is $127,000 to $157,000. These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.

In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). The CCGP is a program designed to offer multi-year cash grants providing for a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute. As soon as reasonably practical after your start date, you will receive a grant letter describing the terms of your award under the CCGP.

title: Building Engineer
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

Arc Institute operates advanced wet-lab and research facilities where uptime directly protects irreplaceable science: cell lines, samples, and instruments representing years of work. We're hiring a hands-on Facilities Building Engineer to own the reliability of our building systems and lab-critical environments. 

This is a working engineer role. You will diagnose and fix problems yourself, and you’ll know when a job calls for a specialist. You will direct our vendor and contract-support partners to get it done right, on time, and on budget. You'll also run facility projects end-to-end and serve as the calm, service-oriented point of contact for the researchers who depend on the building.

About you

  • You catch problems early, before they turn into a researcher’s bad day. You’re just as comfortable running a diagnostic yourself as you are getting a vendor on the phone to handle something that’s not yours to touch. You want to know why a system works the way it does, not just how to patch it.
  • You like being around science, even though you’re not a scientist. You get that a freezer failure here isn’t an inconvenience; it’s years of someone’s work. That weight doesn’t stress you out. It’s part of what makes the job worth doing well.
  • You don’t need a lot of ramp-up time or close supervision to take ownership. You’re comfortable being the primary engineer onsite, you set your own priorities, and you integrate with the team from day one.
  • You’re straightforward and easy to track down. You build trust through consistent follow-through.

 

In this position you will

  • Serve as the primary onsite contact for facilities service requests; deliver responsive, professional service to researchers and staff.
  • Operate and maintain lab HVAC systems serving wet labs — air-change rates, pressure cascades/room differentials, VAV/reheat, fume-hood and BSC exhaust — and respond to alarms before they threaten research.
  • Support lab utilities: RO/DI and lab-water loops, lab gases (CO₂, N₂, compressed air, vacuum), acid-neutralization systems, eyewash/safety-shower testing.
  • Coordinate biosafety-adjacent equipment maintenance (fume-hood face-velocity checks, BSC recertification) with EH&S (Environmental Health & Safety).
  • Self-perform routine multi-trade work (HVAC/mechanical troubleshooting, plumbing, electrical, and general building repairs) within your qualifications and licensing
  • Interpret and adjust the building automation system (e.g., Alerton, Automated Logic, Johnson Controls, Siemens)
  • Exercise sound judgment on when to self-perform vs. engage a specialist
  • Maintain standby-power readiness: generator, ATS, and UPS testing supporting freezers and critical loads.
  • Run small-to-mid facility projects (renovations, equipment installs, system upgrades): scope, budget, contractor coordination, and closeout.
  • Support compliance with Cal/OSHA requirements (IIPP, LOTO, confined space, hot work), NFPA 70E, fire and life-safety codes and testing, California building, mechanical, plumbing, and electrical codes, and Title 24
  • Support compliance with Bay Area Air Quality Management District (BAAQMD) permits for generators and boilers, and with CUPA, hazardous materials, and wastewater-discharge requirements
  • Align building operations with CDC/NIH BMBL biosafety guidance in coordination with EH&S.
  • Drive energy efficiency and monitoring across high-load systems (compute/cooling, freezer farm), identifying sustainability and cost-reduction opportunities.

Requirements

  • 5+ years operating and maintaining building mechanical systems in a life-sciences, commercial, or institutional facility, including direct HVAC troubleshooting experience
  • Demonstrated ability to self-perform routine work across mechanical/HVAC (deep expertise), plumbing, electrical, and general construction, with sound judgment on when to escalate specialized work to vendors
  • Proven ability to direct and manage the quality of vendors and contract support
  • Ability to read mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) drawings; proficiency with BMS/BAS and CMMS software
  • EPA 608 Universal refrigerant certification
  • Valid California driver's license
  • Willingness to participate in a shared after-hours on-call rotation for lab-critical systems, including responding onsite when needed
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs

Preferred Qualifications

  • Degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering preferred; equivalent hands-on experience may be substituted
  • Experience in a BSL-2 research or vivarium environment
  • Journey-level trade credential or Stationary Engineer certification (e.g., IUOE/Stationary Engineers Local 39)
  • OSHA 30, boiler operator, or backflow tester certification
  • Experience with -80°C freezer farms and cryogenic systems
  • Experience supporting asset-replacement and capital-planning processes
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish, to support coordination with trades and vendor teams

The base salary range for this position is $107,000 to $132,000. title: Patient Care Coordinator
description:
SERC Physical Therapy, a brand partner of Upstream Rehabilitation, is looking for a Patient Care Coordinator to join our team in Spring Hill, KS

 

Are you looking for a position in a growing organization where you can make a significant impact on the lives of others? 

What is a Patient Care Coordinator?

  • A Patient Care Coordinator is an entry-level office role that is responsible for maintaining pleasant and consistent daily operations of the clinic.
  • Our Patient Care Coordinators have excellent customer service skills.
  • Patient Care Coordinators learn new things – a lot! The Patient Care Coordinator multitasks in multiple computer programs each day.

A day in the life of a Patient Care Coordinator:

  • Greets everyone who enters the clinic in a friendly and welcoming manner.
  • Schedules new referrals received by fax or by telephone from patients, physician offices.
  • Verifies insurance coverage for patients.
  • Collects patient payments.
  • Maintains an orderly and organized front office workspace.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Fulltime positions include:

  • Annual paid Charity Day to give back to a cause meaningful to you
  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • 3-week Paid Time Off plus paid holidays
  • 401K + company match

Position Summary:

The Patient Care Coordinator - I (PCC-I) supports clinic growth through excellence in execution of the practice management role and patient intake processes. This individual will work in collaboration with the Clinic Director (CD) to carry out efficient clinic procedures. The PCC-I position is responsible for supporting the mission, vision, and values of Upstream Rehabilitation. 

 

Responsibilities:

  • Core responsibilities
    • Collect all money due at the time of service
    • Convert referrals into evaluations
    • Schedule patient visits
    • Customer Service
  • Create an inviting clinic atmosphere.
  • Make all welcome calls
    • Monitor and influence arrival rate through creation of a great customer experience
  • Practice Management
    • Manage schedule efficiently 
    • Manage document routing 
    • Manage personal overtime 
    • Manage non-clinical documentation 
    • Manage deposits
    • Manage caseload, D/C candidate, progress note, and insurance reporting
    • Monitor clinic inventory
  • Training
    • o Attend any required training with the Territory Field Trainers (TFT) for Raintree and other business process updates. 
    • Complete quarterly compliance training.                                                                 

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Communication skills – must be able to relate well to Business Office and Field leadership
  • Ability to multitask, organizational detail, ability to meet deadlines, work with little to no supervision
  • As a member of a team, must possess efficient time management and presentation skills

Physical Requirements:

  • This position is subject to inside environmental conditions: protections from weather conditions but not necessarily from temperature changes; exposed to noise consistent with indoor environment.
  • This is a full-time position operating within normal business hours Monday through Friday, with an expectation of minimum of 40 hours per week; May be required to attend special events some evenings and weekends, or work additional hours as needed.

title: Literacy Coach
description:
About the Team

Michigan Online School (MOS) is a K-12 tuition-free online public school in the state of Michigan. At MOS, we empower students to be their best by enabling them to learn in ways that are right for them – using innovative technology at home, at their proper level, and at their own pace.

The Literacy Coach partners with teachers, school leaders, and instructional teams to strengthen literacy instruction and improve student achievement. Through job-embedded coaching, professional learning, collaborative planning, classroom modeling, and data-informed support, the Literacy Coach helps educators implement evidence-based literacy practices aligned with Michigan academic standards and state literacy initiatives.

The Literacy Coach works collaboratively with teachers, principals, leadership teams, and data specialists to build instructional capacity, support effective literacy interventions, strengthen reading outcomes, and promote continuous school improvement. This position emphasizes a collaborative, relationship-driven approach to professional growth and instructional excellence.

Eligibility: Open to residents of Michigan

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Instructional Coaching & Teacher Support

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with teaching staff grounded in mutual respect, teamwork, and accountability.

  • Partner with classroom teachers to implement evidence-based early literacy instructional practices through job-embedded coaching.

  • Provide individualized and small-group coaching through classroom observations, instructional modeling, co-teaching, collaborative planning, goal-setting, and reflective conversations.

  • Model effective whole-group and small-group literacy instruction for teachers and students.

  • Support teachers in developing effective classroom literacy environments and implementing research-based instructional strategies and literacy programs.

  • Coach teachers in structured literacy lesson design and the implementation of practices aligned with state standards.

  • Provide ongoing feedback to help teachers reflect on, establish goals, practice, and refine instructional skills aligned with the Essential Instructional Practices in Literacy.

Data Analysis & Student Achievement

  • Analyze formative assessment, screening, and diagnostic data to develop and inform instructional plans.

  • Support teachers in collecting, analyzing, and using student data to guide instructional decisions and improve learning outcomes.

  • Administer and interpret universal screeners to identify students with characteristics of dyslexia.

  • Train and support teachers in identifying reading deficiencies and implementing appropriate evidence-based interventions.

  • Support the identification and implementation of instructional strategies to address students' individual literacy needs.

Professional Learning & School Leadership

  • Lead, organize, and facilitate professional learning communities (PLCs) and collaborative professional development opportunities for teachers.

  • Facilitate the school's literacy leadership committee and support the development of a comprehensive literacy continuum.

  • Assist building principals in identifying instructional strengths and areas of need related to literacy instruction.

  • Communicate student progress, instructional needs, and coaching outcomes with principals and school leadership teams.

  • Attend required coaching trainings, networking sessions, and professional learning opportunities.

  • Engage in continuous professional learning to remain current on research-supported literacy instruction, coaching practices, and the science of reading.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Valid Michigan teaching certificate.

  • Five or more years of successful teaching experience; virtual teaching experience preferred.

  • Experience facilitating professional learning at the grade-level or team level.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting students with dyslexia or characteristics of dyslexia, including the implementation of evidence-based reading interventions.

  • Training or certification in a dyslexia-focused instructional program.

  • Strong knowledge of reading and writing development, literacy acquisition, and evidence-based instructional practices.

  • Familiarity with Michigan's Dyslexia Handbook and state requirements related to early screening and intervention.

  • Knowledge of current Michigan literacy standards and legislation, including Public Acts 146 and 147.

  • Experience using formative assessments, universal screeners, and diagnostic assessment tools to inform instructional planning.

  • Ability to use classroom observation data and formative assessment practices to guide instructional coaching and professional learning.

  • Proficiency with technology-based instructional and organizational tools.

  • Demonstrated ability to build positive professional relationships and collaborate effectively with teachers, administrators, and other stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Literacy or a related field, or Reading Specialist certification.

  • LETRS training or equivalent professional learning focused on research-based early literacy practices and the science of reading.

  • Additional training or certification in evidence-based structured literacy instruction.

About Us

“We believe that every child should be able to be anything they want in life, regardless of their birthplace and circumstances.” – Ron Packard, CEO & Founder

ACCEL Schools is a network of 80+ high-performing, public charter schools serving PK-12 students. We proudly advocate for school choice and work to address educational inequities throughout the United States. Our schools are inclusive and widely differ to reflect the unique values of the many urban, suburban, and rural communities we serve. Our brick-and-mortar, virtual, and hybrid schools specialize in closing educational gaps and offer innovative models such as career-technical education, sports training, bilingual programming, and more. We have been recognized and praised by legislators, authorizers, and researchers for providing exceptional education options to students in historically under-resourced communities.

 We offer the following benefits:

 Life benefits – time & peace of mind

  • Paid time off

title: Data Management Consultant, IDSR in Private Health Facilities
description:
Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) is a global health organization that partners locally and globally to create and scale solutions to the world’s deadliest health threats. Millions of people die from preventable health threats. We collaborate to close the gap between proven, life-saving solutions and the people who need them. Since 2017, we’ve worked with governments and other partners in more than 60 countries to save millions of lives. We work toward a future where people live longer, healthier lives, communities flourish, and economies thrive. This is an ambitious vision, and it inspires us and our partners to make progress every day. 

In partnership with the World Health Organization, Ethiopia’s Federal Ministry of Health (FMoH), and the Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI), Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) has been implementing Strengthening IDSR in Private Health Facilities. The project supports private health facilities to prevent, detect, and respond to public health threats while maintaining essential health services through core interventions of capacity building, longitudinal mentorship, supportive supervision, monitoring of key indicators, and data use to guide tailored interventions at the facility level.

Length of Engagement: 4 months. The contracting and commencement of the assignment are contingent on confirmation and availability of funding.

Level of Effort: Equivalent to FTE

Location: Remote with travel as stated within Ethiopia

Job Structure: Independent Contractor 

  • Must have a registered business license to operate as a consultant in Ethiopia, or be willing to get one before the contract is signed.

Position Summary

The Data Management Consultant will support expansion into additional facilities and strengthen ongoing project implementation across 13 regions. The Data Management Consultant will work with the Regional Implementation Consultants and provide cross-cutting data management, quality assurance, analysis, visualization, and reporting support across all participating regions. 

The consultant will ensure that data generated through facility assessments, training, mentorship, supportive supervision, and routine project monitoring are complete, accurate, timely, appropriately managed, analyzed, visualized, and used to inform implementation and decision-making.

The Data Management Consultant will support implementation across all project regions and will work closely with the four Regional Implementation Consultants, the Principal Manager for Prevent Epidemics, and the Epidemic Ready Primary Health Care (ERPHC) Technical Advisor to achieve all deliverables. 

Core Tasks and Activities

Digital Data Collection Tools and Systems 

  • Support the set-up, review, testing, and configuration,  of ODK-based data collection tools used for mentorship, supportive supervision, and other project monitoring activities. 
  • Update facility master lists, facility codes, regional identifiers, and other reference information required for standardized data collection and reporting across project regions. 
  • Orient and provide technical support to Regional Implementation Consultants, assessors, mentors, mentees, and other relevant project participants on the appropriate use of ODK and other digital data-collection and reporting tools. 
  • Provide technical support and troubleshooting for data collection, submission, correction, and management throughout project implementation. 

 Data Management and Data Quality Assurance 

  • Support the development and implementation of project data-management procedures, including data cleaning, validation, organization, documentation, storage, and quality assurance. 
  • Assess data submitted from all participating regions and facilities for data completeness, timeliness, consistency, validity, duplication, and missing information. 
  • Clean, consolidate, and manage data received from all participating regions and maintain updated project datasets throughout the implementation period. 
  • Identify data-quality issues and work closely with the Regional Implementation Consultants and relevant regional teams to correct identified gaps and improve data quality. 
  • Review mentorship data submitted each month and provide timely data-quality feedback to the Regional Implementation Consultants and project team to support corrective action. 
  • Support data-quality spot checks and verification of selected facility data, as needed, to ensure that data submitted through project monitoring tools are consistent with facility records. 

Data Analysis and Visualization 

  • Analyze  baseline assessments, mentorship data, supportive supervision data, endline assessments, and other relevant project monitoring data. 
  • Develop,  and  update Power BI dashboards and other agreed data-visualization products to monitor progress across regions and facilities. 
  • Analyze and visualize key project indicators, including implementation coverage, mentorship progress, PHEM and IPC performance, facility improvements, data completeness and timeliness, and other relevant indicators. 
  • Prepare regional and overall data summaries, tables, charts, and other analytical outputs for routine project monitoring, performance review meetings, and decision-making. 
  • Support Regional Implementation Consultants and the project team in interpreting project data and identifying implementation gaps, trends, areas requiring follow-up, and opportunities for course correction. 

Project Monitoring and Reporting 

  • Provide data and analytical inputs to monthly project progress reports, Pandemic Fund reporting requirements, performance review meetings, and other project reporting needs. 
  • Support endline data consolidation and analysis, including comparison of baseline and endline performance and documentation of changes in PHEM and IPC indicators across participating facilities and regions. 

Documentation, Handover, and Sustainability 

  • Maintain organized and secure project datasets, data-collection tools, analytical files, dashboards, and relevant data-management documentation throughout the consultancy. 
  • Prepare and hand over final cleaned datasets, data dictionaries, data-collection tools, dashboards, analytical outputs, and other agreed data-management products at the end of the contract. 
  • Support additional data-management, monitoring, analysis, visualization, and reporting activities within the scope of and relevant to the project as agreed with the ERPHC Technical Advisor. 
  • Strengthen regional capacity and facilitate the handover of data management processes, including the development of region-specific plans for data management systems and data use, to ensure a smooth transition and sustained system functionality after the project close out. 

Contract Deliverables

The Data Management Consultant will be responsible for the following key deliverables: 

  • Project data-management system established and maintained, including reviewed and tested ODK data-collection tools, facility master lists/codes, data organization structures, and data-quality procedures. 
  • Relevant project staff and implementation teams supported on digital data collection, including orientation and technical support on ODK, data submission, correction, and data-quality requirements. 
  • Monthly mentorship and project-monitoring data consolidated and quality-assured, including  monitoring of data completeness, timeliness, validity, consistency, duplication, and missing information. 
  • Power BI dashboard maintained and updated to visualize key project indicators and implementation progress across participating regions and facilities. 
  • Monthly data analysis and visualization completed, with appropriate summary tables, charts, dashboards, and analytical inputs provided for project monitoring, performance review meetings, and monthly reporting. 
  • Data-quality issues identified, documented, and communicated to Regional Implementation Consultants and the project team, with appropriate follow-up and correction supported. 
  • Data and analytical inputs provided for final project reporting, including regional and overall performance summaries, trends, achievements, gaps, and relevant visualizations. 
  • Final project data package completed and handed over, including final cleaned datasets, data dictionary, ODK forms, dashboard files, analysis outputs, and relevant data-management documentation. 

Contract Management

The Consultant will submit deliverables to the ERPHC Technical Advisor for review and acceptance. The Principal Manager for Prevent Epidemics will manage the contract and approve invoices. 

Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, health informatics, monitoring and evaluation, data science, health information systems, or a related field. 
  • 5+ years of relevant experience in public health data management, monitoring and evaluation, epidemiology, health information systems, disease surveillance, or related areas. 
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience in managing, cleaning, validating, analyzing, and visualizing public health or health-program data. 
  • Hands-on experience with ODK/ODK Central or comparable electronic data-collection platforms, including form testing, data management, export, cleaning, and troubleshooting. 
  • Experience with Power BI dashboards, including development or maintenance of dashboards and visualization of program-monitoring indicators. 
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience using statistical or analytical software such as R, Stata, SPSS, Python, or other comparable tools. 
  • Experience conducting and documenting data-quality assurance, including assessment of data completeness, timeliness, validity, consistency, and accuracy. 
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze and translate data into clear dashboards, tables, charts, summaries, and other products that can support programmatic decision-making. 
  • Strong organizational and data-management skills, with excellent communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with technical and program teams. 
  • Ability to manage and consolidate data from multiple regions and implementation teams while maintaining standardized data-management and quality-assurance procedures. 
  • Proficiency in MS Office applications. 
  • Fluent in English and Amharic. 
  • Willingness and ability to travel within Ethiopia as needed to provide data-management support, participate in relevant project activities, and conduct data-quality verification and supportive supervision. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience working with DHIS2, particularly health surveillance, PHEM, or related health-program data, is an advantage. 
  • Knowledge and understanding of Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR), Public Health Emergency Management (PHEM), Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), or related public health programs is an advantage. 
  • Experience working closely with EPHI and regional counterparts, including Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs) and/or Regional Public Health Institutes (RPHIs), is an advantage. 

Application Process

Interested candidates should submit their CV and a cover letter detailing their suitability for the role.

We encourage applications from and provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, ancestry, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, marital status, organ donor status, or status as a veteran. Resolve to Save Lives complies with all applicable US EEO laws.

title: Scientist II, Screening
description:
Profluent is the frontier AI lab for biology. Profluent builds powerful foundation models for all of life's molecules, unlocking solutions that transform medicine, agriculture, and beyond. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Emeryville, CA, Profluent is backed by leading investors including Altimeter Capital, Bezos Expeditions, Spark Capital, Insight Partners, Air Street Capital, AIX Ventures, and Convergent Ventures and has raised over $150M to date.

The Role

Profluent is seeking a motivated, rigorous, and collaborative scientist to establish and lead a centralized gene editor screening function. High-quality experimental data is a core input to our protein design models, and this role will own the screening operations that produce it.

This role centers on building and running a screening core responsible for assay standardization, data quality, and team development. At first, you will support campaigns that generate training and evaluation data for our protein design models, and the scope may grow to cover more programs. You will design, run, and troubleshoot mammalian genome editing assays with NGS readouts in arrayed and pooled formats. You will set the technical standards that make our data reproducible and trustworthy. You will also build and mentor a team of Research Associates, and coordinate closely with Automation, Bioinformatics, Data Science, and Biology to keep the screening pipeline running smoothly from start to finish.

As a leader of the team, you will balance hands-on scientific execution with people management and process development. You will identify, prioritize, and drive infrastructure projects that improve throughput, consistency, and assay sensitivity. You will also work with leadership to shape the long-term scope of the core.

We welcome candidates from diverse backgrounds who share our commitment to revolutionizing biology, driving meaningful innovation, and making a lasting impact on global healthcare.

This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of AI-driven protein design while collaborating with a dynamic, interdisciplinary team of experts in machine learning, protein engineering, cell biology, and gene editing.

 

Responsibilities

Team Leadership

  • Build and lead a team of 2–4 Research Associates, including hiring, training, performance management, and career development
  • Train and mentor staff on aseptic technique, assay execution, and documentation standards
  • Foster a supportive team culture that prioritizes growth, engagement, and well-being

Execution

  • Prioritize, schedule, and resource cross-functional experiments in coordination with Automation and Bioinformatics
  • Design, execute, troubleshoot, and analyze mammalian genome editing assays with NGS readouts in arrayed and pooled formats
  • Onboard new assays and extend existing assays to new enzyme classes
  • Maintain sample chain of custody from plate mapping through automation, sample preparation, and sequencing submission, partnering with Bioinformatics on data schema and capture
  • Communicate technical results clearly to both expert and non-expert audiences
  • Deliver QC'd, analysis-ready datasets with documented QC flags to ML

Process Development

  • Define and enforce technical standards, and write and maintain SOPs
  • Qualify new assays and define acceptance criteria based on reproducibility data
  • Maintain cell line quality and inventory for screening assays, in coordination with teams that manage cell banks
  • Characterize assay sensitivity, including the minimum detectable difference in activity at standard replicate counts
  • Identify, prioritize, and plan infrastructure projects that continually improve assays and processes
  • Coordinate process development across Automation, Bioinformatics, Data Science, and Biology
  • Evaluate the costs and benefits of centralizing high-throughput workflows in partnership with other teams
  • Work with leadership to assess and refine the scope of core functions

 

Qualifications

  • PhD in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, or a related field and 2+ years of relevant industry experience, or MS in a related field and 10+ years of relevant industry experience
  • Hands-on experience with bacterial and mammalian cell culture, genome editing, and NGS-based assays
  • Experience with high-throughput experimentation and analysis of large datasets
  • Experience with LIMS or ELN systems for sample and experiment tracking
  • Demonstrated ability to establish technical standards and drive consistent execution across operators


Preferences

  • Experience working in or building a core facility or centralized service function
  • Track record of building or improving high-throughput processes
  • Experience leading infrastructure or process improvement projects
  • Experience with liquid handling automation and tech transfer
  • Experience with cell bank and inventory management
  • Strong foundation in experimental design and statistics, including power analysis and design of experiments (DOE)

Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. We measure tumor-derived cfDNA at the molecular level to help inform personalized health care decisions with a non-invasive test.

Natera R&D is seeking a highly motivated Scientist to join the rapidly growing assay development team to help build the future of Natera. In this position, you will work with high-performing cross-functional teams to develop laboratory tests that benefit our patients and the business. The ideal candidate has a deep understanding of molecular biology, strong scientific curiosity, demonstrated experience in developing Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) technologies and proven experience developing and validating assays through the product development cycle. You will plan, execute, and lead scientific studies under design control in a regulated environment, helping to improve and expand Natera’s oncology product portfolio.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Leads in-laboratory efforts and performs duties largely independent from manager 
  • Plan, execute, analyze, and present data from moderate- to high-complexity experiments, including hands-on troubleshooting and root-cause analysis for development, verification and validation studies
  • Coordinate study design, sample size justification, acceptance criteria, and analysis with biostatistics and bioinformatics; perform basic data analysis (e.g., Excel, JMP) 
  • Characterize analytical performance studies following CLSI guidance 
  • Author and review SOPs, protocols, study reports, and transfer documents for production implementation; contribute to design control deliverables (design inputs/outputs, risk assessments per ISO 14971) in line with CLIA, CAP, 21 CFR Part 820/QMSR, and ISO 13485
  • Communicates progress directly with colleagues and senior management. Provides regular updates, outcomes, risks, and next steps at laboratory and department meetings
  • Documents research progress under an Electronic Quality Management System
  • Train junior team members on new SOPs and laboratory workflows, and provide technical guidance and troubleshooting support to laboratory operations
  • Be flexible to lead multiple studies and laboratory priorities while maintaining targeted timelines; perform other duties as assigned
  • Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire
  • Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements

Qualifications

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of high-throughput NGS workflows or other clinical genetic testing applications, required

Gaining a deep understanding of the single cell market and Parse’s products will be critical to success. 

TERRITORY AND TRAVEL

You will ideally be based in the Greater Boston Area, covering academic accounts in the area.  The position will require travel approximately 50% of the time, most of which will be day trips. Minimal overnight stays.

IN THIS POSITION, YOU WILL

  • Generate and manage both high volume and large complex sales
  • Ensure customers are satisfied and making rapid experimental progress
  • Develop, maintain, and grow repeat business while maintaining strong relationships
  • Prospect effectively to generate an immediate, medium, and long-term sales pipelines to ensure consistent quota obtainment
  • Negotiate and close deals while minimizing discounting
  • Effectively communicate technical advantages to customers
  • Develop a quarterly and yearly business plan that incorporates both strategic and tactical activities
  • Prioritize and qualify inbound leads
  • Provide management with insight on competition, market trends, and customer feedback
  • Manage your sales funnel with a high degree of accuracy
  • Leverage expertise of Field Application Scientists to support customers and drive sales
  • Leverage expertise of prospecting specialists to maximize customer meetings and drive new sales
  • Use CRM to manage and track deals
  • Continue to develop technical knowledge related to new, emerging, and related single cell research
  • Forecast projected sales in your territory
  • Display a high degree of professionalism both internally and externally

FOR THIS POSITION, WE LOOK FOR

  • Bachelors in biology/genomics or a related field. A Masters or PhD is a plus
  • Minimum of 1 year of field sales experience in NGS and/or genomics-related products or services, including both account management and new business development.
  • Experience successfully selling to local academic accounts, ideally including genomic core facilities
  • Previous molecular biology lab experience is preferred
  • Excellent communication skills - written and verbal
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time (locally, nationally, and internationally as needed)

We use evolution to structure, explore, and engineer biology. Our Deployment team applies Arcadia’s novel, validated platform and instrument technologies to bench research. The role

We're hiring a scientist with deep hands-on expertise in molecular and cell biology. As part of the Deployment team at Arcadia, you'll help us build our experimental assets and operating principles. You will take our most critical, unique approaches and make them robust and scalable. You'll work side-by-side with software and instrument engineers. The data you generate will, in many cases, inform models directly as we build towards several agentic lab-in-the-loop workflows that leverage Arcadia’s novel platform capabilities.

  • Experience with high-dimensional phenotypic readouts

General

  • Familiarity with agentic workflows and coding practices
  • Disciplined data and documentation habits: consistent formats, complete metadata, and protocols that a colleague or an automated system can run as written
  • Clear written and verbal communication with collaborators outside your area of expertise

Nice to have

  • People or project management experience
  • Experience working with high-dimensional data, including advising on how data should be structured, upholding statistical rigor, and guiding collaborators on what the results can and can’t support

title: Research Associate 2
description:
LOCATION: On-Site in Boulder, CO (Foresight Dx business unit, a Natera company)

 

ABOUT OUR COMPANY:

Foresight Diagnostics is a molecular diagnostics company pioneering non-invasive cancer detection through highly sensitive, cell-free DNA-based liquid biopsy technologies. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer. 

We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. It’s an exciting moment to join us. 

Headquartered in Boulder, Colorado, our team operates in a high accountability, collaborative environment where quality and continuous improvement aren’t just values - they’re how we work every day.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Every liquid biopsy result starts at the bench, and this role puts you right there. As part of our Boulder R&D team, you’ll work hands-on with scientists developing ultrasensitive, cell-free DNA technology designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment for patients with cancer. You’ll run experiments across the NGS workflow, from gDNA isolation and library prep to hybrid capture and sequencing, using automated liquid handlers and instruments like the TapeStation and Qubit. Along the way, you’ll learn to troubleshoot, keep instruments running smoothly, and understand why an experiment behaves the way it does, not just how to run it.

You won’t work in a silo. You’ll partner daily with Associates and Scientists, summarize and present your data to the team, and write SOPs that shape how we work. Your notebooks, results, and attention to detail will be trusted and relied on by the people around you. Foresight’s Stanford-born science now has the backing of Natera, a global leader in cell-free DNA testing, so you’ll get the agility of a mission-driven startup with the resources and reach of an established company. If you have a few years of molecular biology experience and want to build deep expertise in one of the most exciting areas of modern diagnostics, in a collaborative, high-accountability culture where quality and continuous improvement are part of everyday work, we’d love to meet you.

 

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

You will work primarily with R&D assisting Associates/Scientists in various lab duties. Responsibilities will include:

  • Independently execute simple experiments and perform basic troubleshooting 
  • Produce competent, reproducible results to a high technical standard
  • Maintain accurate and well-organized laboratory records, worksheets and notebooks
  • Summarize data in spreadsheets, graphs and presentations
  • Write standard operating procedures (SOP) and other lab-related documents as needed
  • Maintain equipment and instruments in good operating condition, recognize any malfunctions and troubleshoot as needed
  • Utilize molecular biology techniques in performing laboratory tests. This role will have occasional access to PHI both in paper and electronic form and have occasional access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job.
  • Adhere to environmental, health and safety (EHS) guidelines and good laboratory practices (GLP)
  • Perform other tasks as specified by the manager/director

 

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS/BA in a biological science or equivalent
  • Minimum of 2 years Molecular Biology laboratory experience required

 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • gDNA isolation from biological samples (preferred).
  • Experience with library preparation for next generation sequencing and sequencing platforms 
  • Experience with hybrid capture technologies
  • Experience with laboratory automated liquid handler platforms
  • Sample analysis/QC on the Agilent Tapestation, Nanodrop, Qubit, electrophoresis
  • Must have proven interpersonal, communication, computer, and technical skills.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills required.
  • Microsoft Excel experience required

Compensation & Total Rewards 

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

  • Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Generous paid time off and company holidays
  • Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range 

$74,800.00 - $89,000.00

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA testing, transforming how disease is detected and managed across Women’s Health, Oncology, Organ Health, and Rare Disease. Our work depends on world-class laboratories, and keeping those labs safe is central to our mission.

Start your EHS career at the heart of a high-growth genomics company.   • Regular computer and telephone use, and ability to read printed material
